```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`read_runner()`, `plot_runner()`, and `runner_shiny()` work with simulations
generated by the [LPJ-GUESS Runner](https://github.com/hie-dave/lpjg-gui/). They
use the runner's R interface to discover generated simulations and to read their
files. Install the `lpjguessRunner` package using its [installation
instructions](https://github.com/hie-dave/lpjg-gui/tree/master/r). Reading
existing outputs does not execute the model or invoke the .NET runner.

These functions assume that the simulations completed successfully.

## Plot outputs

Outputs from runner-generated simulations may be plotted with the
`plot_runner()` function:

```{r plot-outputs}
library(lpjguessOutput)
directory <- "/path/to/runner-output"
plot_runner(directory, "dave_lai")
```

## Read outputs

```{r read-outputs}
lai <- read_runner(directory, "dave_lai")
lai <- read_runner(directory, "file_dave_lai")
lai <- read_runner(directory, "dave_lai.out")
lai
#       Lon    Lat       Date stand patch variable value
#     <num>  <num>     <POSc> <int> <int>   <fctr> <num>
# 1: 150.72 -33.62 2014-01-01     0     0    total     0
# 2: 150.72 -33.62 2014-01-02     0     0    total     0
# 3: 150.72 -33.62 2014-01-03     0     0    total     0
```

The result is a long-form `data.table`: `variable` identifies a column in the
raw output file, and `value` holds its value. Available [model dimensions](output_dimensions.html),
including coordinates, stands, patches, PFTs, individuals, and soil layers,
remain columns. Each file is reshaped before combining it with other files, so
absent measurement columns do not create extra rows. The returned `data.table`
also contains the following columns which can be used to disambiguate a row when
reading multiple columns, outputs, simulations, or instruction files:

- `run_id`: full path to the simulation directory
- `simulation`: simulation name supplied to the runner
- `instruction_file`: ins file basename without extension
- `base_ins`: absolute path to the base/original instruction file
- `ins_file`: absolute path to the generated instruction file
- `simulation_key`: same as `simulation`(??)
- `output`: output file stem
- `output_file`: output file basename
- `output_path`: absolute path to the output file
- `param:*`: one column per parameter override, with the override value. E.g.
  `param:nindiv_max`, `param:pft:MRS:sla`, etc. Missing overrides are `NA`.

Every row retains `run_id`, `simulation`, `instruction_file`, `simulation_key`,
`base_ins`, `ins_file`, `output`, `output_file`, and `output_path`. The `run_id`
is the absolute simulation directory; it distinguishes jobs with identical
names or manifest keys. Moving an experiment changes these absolute paths.

## Work with specific simulations

```{r choose-jobs}
library(lpjguessOutput)

runs <- lpjguessRunner::list_simulations(directory)
runs[c("simulation", "instruction_file", "base_ins", "path")]
#            simulation instruction_file                      base_ins
# 1 nindiv_max_0_sla_26  CumberlandPlain /original/CumberlandPlain.ins
# 2 nindiv_max_1_sla_39  CumberlandPlain /original/CumberlandPlain.ins
# 3 nindiv_max_0_sla_26            Warra           /original/Warra.ins
# 4 nindiv_max_1_sla_39            Warra           /original/Warra.ins
#                                             path
# 1 /generated/CumberlandPlain/nindiv_max_0_sla_26
# 2 /generated/CumberlandPlain/nindiv_max_1_sla_39
# 3           /generated/Warra/nindiv_max_0_sla_26
# 4           /generated/Warra/nindiv_max_1_sla_39

```

All three runner-related functions accept an output-directory path, runner
settings, a `lpjguess_result`, or a simulation table. A table can be filtered
using ordinary R before passing it to the reader or plotter:

```{r filtered-catalog}
selected <- subset(runs, instruction_file == "CumberlandPlain")
lai <- read_runner(selected, "dave_lai")
```

Alternatively, supply `simulations` and `instruction_files` filters:

```{r job-filters}
lai <- read_runner(directory, "dave_lai",
                   instruction_files = "CumberlandPlain",
                   simulations = c("baseline", "high_sla"))
```

## Inspect and filter parameter overrides

```{r inspect-parameters}
parameters <- runner_parameters(runs)
parameters[, c("simulation", "instruction_file", "parameter", "value")]
#             simulation instruction_file   parameter  value
#                 <char>           <char>      <char> <char>
# 1: nindiv_max_0_sla_26  CumberlandPlain  nindiv_max      0
# 2: nindiv_max_0_sla_26  CumberlandPlain pft:MRS:sla     26
# 3: nindiv_max_1_sla_39  CumberlandPlain  nindiv_max      1
# 4: nindiv_max_1_sla_39  CumberlandPlain pft:MRS:sla     39
# 5: nindiv_max_0_sla_26            Warra  nindiv_max      0
# 6: nindiv_max_0_sla_26            Warra pft:MRS:sla     26
# 7: nindiv_max_1_sla_39            Warra  nindiv_max      1
# 8: nindiv_max_1_sla_39            Warra pft:MRS:sla     39

lai <- read_runner(runs, "dave_lai",
                   parameters = list("pft:MRS:sla" = c(26, 39)))
```

Top-level parameter identifiers use their names, such as `nindiv_max`.
Block-scoped identifiers include the block type and name, such as `pft:MRS:sla`.

Manifest factors describe overrides, not all effective settings. A missing
override remains `NA` and is labelled **Not overridden** in plots. Its inherited
base value is not inferred. Select missing overrides with:

```{r missing-override}
lai <- read_runner(runs, "dave_lai",
                   parameters = list("pft:MRS:sla" = NA_character_))
```

The parameter must be known somewhere in the supplied catalog. When several
parameters vary together, a plot coloured by one parameter still compares the
complete simulation recipes.

## Plot and compare simulations

```{r compare-simulations}
plot_runner(runs, "dave_lai", columns = "total")

plot_runner(runs, "dave_lai", columns = "total",
            facet = c("instruction_file", "output"), colour = "simulation")

plot_runner(runs, "dave_lai", columns = "total",
            facet = c("instruction_file", "param:nindiv_max"),
            colour = "param:pft:MRS:sla")
```

Available dimensions are `column`, `instruction_file`, `simulation`, `output`,
`run_id`, [model dimensions present in the files](output_dimensions.html), and the `param:*` columns.
Lines from different jobs remain separate even if their colour and facet values
match.

With `columns = NULL` (the default), the plotter selects measurement columns
shared by every selected file. Supply `columns` explicitly to compare different
variables in heterogeneous files. The default panels show instruction file,
output, and column, with colour distinguishing simulations.

## Freshness and unavailable files

Freshness is computed independently for every simulation/instruction-file job.
Within that job's output directory, files more than `stale_threshold_secs`
seconds behind its newest `.out` file are stale; the default window is 10
seconds. All discovered `.out` files contribute to the comparison, including
outputs not selected for plotting.

By default, missing, stale, empty, or unreadable requested outputs produce an
error identifying the affected jobs. To intentionally read available files:

```{r partial-reads}
lai <- read_runner(runs, "dave_lai", missing = "warn")
lai <- read_runner(runs, "dave_lai", missing = "ignore")
lai <- read_runner(runs, "dave_lai", stale_threshold_secs = Inf)
```

An empty selection, or a file containing a header but no rows always errors.

## Explore interactively

```{r explorer}
runner_shiny(directory)
runner_shiny(selected, refresh_interval = 0, launch.browser = FALSE)
runner_shiny()  # Choose an output directory in the app
```

The explorer requires the `shiny` and `plotly` packages.

Plot controls match `plot_runner()`. Hover for details, zoom, and select legend
entries; download the static plot as PNG/PDF or plotted data as CSV. **R code**
shows a concise `plot_runner()` call using the output directory, with filters
and plot options included only where needed. The app initially selects all
instruction files and simulations, matching the plotting API defaults:

```{r default-export}
library(lpjguessOutput)
plot_runner("/path/to/runner-output", "dave_lai")
```

The generated code preserves the selected jobs, parameter filters, columns,
and plot settings. When the app was given a simulation table instead of a
directory, the code includes that selected table as a `runs` object.

Files are checked every five seconds and when **Refresh files** is clicked.
Unchanged snapshots reuse cached data, and plot-control changes do not reread
files. Directory/settings/result inputs rediscover catalog entries on refresh;
an explicitly supplied simulation table retains its chosen set of jobs.
Set `refresh_interval = 0` to disable periodic checks.

## Further reading

Read [Understanding output dimensions](output_dimensions.html) for the shared
explanation of measurements, model identifiers, facets, and colours. The
[DAVE plotting guide](plotting_dave.html#plot-a-layered-soil-output) also provides
worked examples of soil-layer plots and custom plots from long-form data.
